root_cause: The opt-125m-gptq model export test failed accuracy validation when comparing OV-exported outputs against framework (PyTorch) reference outputs. The model is loaded via GPT-QModel (6.0.3) with TorchFusedQuantLinear kernel, converted through the PyTorch FX frontend (TorchFXPythonDecoder), and the resulting ov::Model inference results diverge from the PyTorch baseline. This is a deterministic correctness failure — the compare_results function returns False for at least one output tensor pair. The failure is not a timeout and all other test cases passed, isolating the issue to opt_gptq model handling.
reproduction_steps: Run: pytest install/tests/model_hub_tests/pytorch/test_llm.py::TestLLMModel::test_export_model_precommit[CPU-opt_gptq-katuni4ka/opt-125m-gptq] -v after installing OV with PyTorch frontend and GPT-QModel 6.0.3 + transformers 5.5.3
recommended_actions: Inspect the PyTorch FX frontend conversion path for OPT-GPTQ models — check if any recent changes to quantization-related op handling (MatMul, dequantize, etc.) introduced numerical divergence.
Compare OV output tensors vs PyTorch tensors for the opt-125m-gptq logits to determine magnitude of error.
Check if PR #37029 touches the PyTorch frontend or any quantization/GPTQ conversion logic.
If the test was passing before this PR, bisect the PyTorch FX decoder changes.
prevention_strategies: Add tolerance-aware comparison for quantized model exports; ensure GPTQ model accuracy tests are run on affected frontend changes before merge queue entry.
historical_context: This is a recurring failure: 13 occurrences starting 2026-07-27T12:33:21Z. Same test (test_export_model_precommit[CPU-opt_gptq-katuni4ka/opt-125m-gptq]) has been failing across multiple PRs (37029, 36957, 36860). The pattern has been active for over 16 hours.
